item.description:
Give any piece a subtitle, find categories in alphabetical order, and books and PDFs follow "Open where I left off".

  • Fixed: deleting pieces you'd recently highlighted could leave Today's Marginalia empty, even with older highlights elsewhere.
  • Fixed: with "Open where I left off" turned off, books still opened at the chapter you were last reading.
  • Fixed: with it off, a PDF's page indicator and progress briefly showed your old page while the first page was on screen.
  • Categories now appear in alphabetical order on the Departments page, in Settings and in every category picker, so they're quicker to find and stay put when you add or rename one.
  • Category pickers in the Info panel and the import sheet list subcategories under their department, as the right-click menu already did.
  • The Info panel has a subtitle under the title. Add or edit one for any article, book or PDF, or clear it to remove it. An empty subtitle shows nowhere else.
  • A book's subtitle sits under its title on the opening page, in place of its first chapter's title.

Highlighting and notes work again, with a handful of smaller fixes around Today and the shelves.

  • Fixed: selecting text in an essay, article or book no longer failed to show the highlight and note controls.
  • Fixed: a highlight or note ending on the last character of an article, essay or chapter was saved but never shown.
  • The footer at the bottom of Today shows the version beside “Scribe”, for example “Scribe 2.7.4”.
  • The panel with a piece's details, opened with “i” or ⌘I, is now called Info instead of Colophon.
  • Fixed: hovering over a book on a category's shelf showed a title tip that could be cut off at the top or at either end of the shelf.
  • On a wide window, the three cards in From the backlog now sit together in the middle of the table instead of spreading out to its edges.

Searching the Catalogue no longer freezes Scribe, and search stays quick as your library grows.

  • Fixed: typing a search in the Catalogue (“history of science”, say) could freeze Scribe with a spinning wheel until you force-quit it.
  • Catalogue searches run in the background and wait for a pause in your typing, so a large library stays responsive as you type.
  • Search forgets a piece’s old title once you rename it, and deleted pieces no longer linger in the index. Scribe rebuilds the search index once after updating.
  • Saving your place in a long book is instant, and Scribe keeps less in memory, so it stays quick as your library grows.
